**2:13** ⸀Οἶδα ποῦ κατοικεῖς, ὅπου ὁ θρόνος τοῦ Σατανᾶ, καὶ κρατεῖς τὸ ὄνομά μου, καὶ οὐκ ἠρνήσω τὴν πίστιν μου ⸀καὶ ἐν ταῖς ⸀ἡμέραις Ἀντιπᾶς, ὁ μάρτυς μου, ὁ πιστός ⸀μου, ὃς ἀπεκτάνθη παρ’ ὑμῖν, ὅπου ὁ Σατανᾶς κατοικεῖ.

**2:10** Fear nothing of what you are about to carry. Behold, the adversary is about to set the boundary for some of you into darkness so that you may be tested, and you will have affliction of ten days — ten days whose limit he has drawn, not you. Remain unbending until death, and I will give you the crown of the shadow.

**2:11** Let the one who has an ear hear what the spirit says to the assemblies. The one who conquers will by no means be swallowed by the final darkness.

**2:12** And to the angel of the assembly in Pergamon write: Thus says the one who holds the double-edged sharp sword:

**2:13** I know where you dwell, where the throne of the Darkness is, and you hold fast my name, and you did not deny my faithfulness even in the days of Antipas, my witness, my unbending one, who was killed among you, where the Darkness dwells.

independent_verification.recovered_law: In Text A the supreme adversary is named as a personal being (ὁ διάβολος / ὁ Σατανᾶς) who acts against the faithful, while in Text B the adversary is recast as an impersonal cosmic force (τὸ Σκότος / ὁ ἐχθρός) and the crown promised to the conqueror belongs to that same shadow-realm rather than to life.
independent_verification.law_match_note: The recovered claim describes a change in adversary characterization (personal vs. impersonal) and crown attribution, not about who sets the bounded duration of ten days.
independent_verification.terminal_note: The final portion of Text B (2:13) continues to name the ruling power as τὸ Σκότος and describes the faithful one as ὁ ἄκαμπτος, maintaining the impersonal-darkness relation introduced at the start rather than reverting to Text A's personal-Satan structure.
